_about: Did they improve? Dated roster amendments to the plan's section 3 (the plan file and its sha256 unchanged): each added chat model joins the plan's models for validation and the results table (improve_page.read_plan). The harness records the same amendment in improve.json ('amendments', never read); this file is what the page shows. A model is listed once its setup's settings are in v3.db (the harness exports it from then on).

amendments.note: Added 20 Nov: the small models of 2B or less on our own GPU (LFM3-1.7B also with thinking off, Qwen3.5-2B, Raon-1 nano, SmolLM2-1.7B, SmolLM2-360M), under the same rule, lesson prompt, test and schedule, each with the settings of its league setup. For these and LFM3-1.7B, MiniCPM5-2B and Gemma 4 E2B, the first empty test is a validity check: a model with more than 10% invalid answers there (more than 20 of 200) stops and plays no series. Then SmolLM3-3B with thinking on, with the card's sampling (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95), its first empty test a validity check as above; with thinking off it runs the first empty test only, as a format check, and plays no series. On our own GPU, a model whose next lesson call or next game's lessons would not fit its context stops there with that reason; lessons are never shortened to fit.

models.setting: off (format check only: first empty test, no series)

amendments.note: Added 21 Nov: Inkling 2 Mini with thinking on (effort 0.9), under the same rule, lesson prompt, test and schedule, on the server it shares with Logic & Math and other benchmarks (its owner's pinned load; this run neither starts nor stops it), sampled greedily as on Logic & Math (temperature 0), its first empty test a validity check as above. Its letter is read from its own answer after its reasoning: its server cannot continue a prefilled answer after a reasoning block. While that server is away, the model pauses. At effort 0.9, 110 of the first 148 answers used all 32,768 output tokens without naming an option; that run stopped and played no series. It was then rerun at effort 0.5, otherwise unchanged. That rerun also stopped at the validity check: 40 of 200 answers (20%) used all 32,768 output tokens without naming an option, above the 10% invalid-answer limit; it played no series.

Inkling 2 Mini retry order, decided before either retry's first call. A capped answer counts as a trailing loop when a pattern of at most 64 whitespace tokens reproduces at least 80% of its final 512 whitespace tokens. Of the capped answers, effort 0.9 had 31 loops and 79 still reasoning normally; effort 0.5 had 25 loops and 15 still reasoning normally. Combined, 56 of 150 were loops and 94 were still reasoning normally, so the lower-effort retry comes first. First try: effort 0.2, temperature 0 and the same 32,768-token limit. Its first empty run is the 200-position validity check; at most 20 invalid answers passes, then this setup plays the full schedule. If it fails, second try: effort 0.5 with the model card's complete sampling configuration (do_sample true, temperature 1.0, eos token 200006 and pad token 199999; the token ids are properties of the loaded server, and the request changes temperature from 0 to 1.0). The card specifies no top_p, top_k or min_p. This is a different setup from the Logic & Math row, which uses effort 0.9 and temperature 0. Sampling at temperature 1.0 can widen this setup's own three-empty-run spread and therefore raise its improvement threshold. Its first empty run uses the same validity check; if it passes, it plays the full schedule. If both retries fail, Inkling stops and is recorded as unable to take the test; there is no third setting. Exploratory 10-position probe, not a result: effort 0.9 with the card's temperature 1.0 returned 9 valid answers and had 1 answer reach the 32,768-token limit; mean output was about 19,500 tokens, median about 16,000 and the slowest request took 814 seconds. The probe was effort 0.9, not the second retry's effort 0.5. The shared Logic & Math server is not restarted, reloaded or copied, and these retries do not hold up the small-model batch.
